text: How did Straker's overcoat come to the furze-bush?
why: The overcoat is shown at the furze-bush while Straker left the house in his mackintosh (¶32, ¶35), so the question is a plain one the story raises.

text: How did Straker's overcoat come to the furze-bush? — torn off in the struggle
why: Straker 'defended himself vigorously' against his assailants (¶35), so a struggle tearing the coat off is a possibility a reader has reason to consider.

text: How did Straker's overcoat come to the furze-bush? — Straker took it off himself
why: Taking off the coat is a natural alternative to it being torn off, and the story gives no reason to rule it out yet.

text: Who struck the blow that killed Straker? — unknown assailants
why: ¶35 speaks of Straker defending himself against 'his assailants', and the stranger's identity is not yet known, so unknown assailants is a fair possibility.

text: What made the blow to Straker's head?
why: ¶35 says the head was shattered by a savage blow from some heavy weapon, so asking what made it is a plain question.

text: What made the cut on Straker's thigh?
why: ¶35 describes a long, clean cut on the thigh inflicted by a very sharp instrument, so asking what made it is a plain question.

text: What made the cut on Straker's thigh? — an assailant's very sharp instrument
why: ¶35 says the cut was made by some very sharp instrument while Straker was attacked by assailants, so attributing it to an assailant's instrument is a reasonable possibility.
